Title: Dara, Amoi and Kelat healthy, not abused at Japanese zoo — Taiping council
Article:
IPOH: The Taiping Municipal Council (MPT) has rejected allegations of neglect and abuse involving three elephants transferred to a Japanese zoo, saying their behaviour does not necessarily indicate mental distress.
Its president, Mohamed Akmal Dahalan, said the elephants — Dara, Amoi and Kelat — were in good health and had adapted well to their new surroundings since arriving in Japan in March.
He said the latest reports from the zoo, alongside MPT's assessment, showed that all three elephants were active and in satisfactory overall condition.
"The three elephants have also been reunited since Sept 20 and have unrestricted access to the entire exhibition area and their night enclosures," he said in a statement.
Akmal said MPT took note of concerns raised on social media over the elephants' head-swaying behaviour, alleged zoochosis and the frequency of musth episodes, which had prompted questions about their mental and emotional well-being.
"In this regard, MPT wishes to reiterate that such behaviour should not be directly interpreted as signs of stress, depression or compromised animal welfare. MPT also denies any allegations of neglect or abuse involving the elephants.
"Head-swaying, in particular, cannot be directly interpreted as a sign of stress, as it may also indicate food-anticipation behaviour, in which an animal anticipates being fed," he said.
On Kelat's musth episodes, Akmal said the elephant had entered the phase twice since arriving in Japan, in May and September this year.
He acknowledged that Kelat had lost weight during both episodes but said this was normal. Its weight had since increased and was approaching the level recorded before the second episode in September.
Akmal also dismissed allegations that hormones had been injected into Kelat to increase the frequency of its musth episodes, describing the claims as untrue.
He said all three elephants were given a complete and balanced diet tailored to their nutritional needs, prepared by the zoo's animal care team and monitored by veterinary officers.
"Their diet includes hay, bamboo shoots, fresh grass, vegetables, specially formulated elephant pellets, alfalfa cubes, wheat bran, carrots, sweet potatoes, bread, pineapple tops and fruits such as apples. Salt and vitamins are also given daily," he said.
Akmal said Kelat had gained 580kg since arriving in Japan, while Dara had gained 575kg and Amoi 405kg.
He said the weight gains indicated that their food intake and health were satisfactory.
"Tennoji Zoo also conducts regular enrichment programmes involving varied activities, food and feeding methods to support the elephants' welfare and mental well-being," he added.
Akmal said the zoo remained committed to ensuring that the elephants' nutrition, veterinary care, safety and daily management complied with international standards and best practices.
While respecting the public's right to voice concerns, he urged people to ensure that allegations about the elephants' welfare were supported by credible information and professional assessments.
He said unsubstantiated claims could cause misunderstandings and potentially affect the country's conservation efforts and international cooperation.
"MPT will continue monitoring the elephants' health and welfare and providing updates to ensure the public receives accurate information," he added.

Title: Human Resources Ministry lodges reports over alleged meddling in TalentCorp review
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Human Resources Ministry has lodged several reports with the authorities over alleged attempts to interfere with an ongoing review and investigation at Talent Corporation Malaysia Bhd (TalentCorp).
In a statement, the ministry said the interference included spreading misleading information, attempting to influence individuals within the agency and diverting attention from matters under scrutiny.
It said such actions could undermine the integrity and independence of the review and investigation.
The reports were lodged after the ministry received information and evidence, allowing the authorities to conduct an independent investigation.
"The ministry will leave it entirely to the authorities to examine the evidence, establish the facts and take appropriate legal action if warranted." it said.
The ministry and TalentCorp are undertaking organisational reforms to strengthen the agency's transparency, integrity and accountability.
A joint review by TalentCorp's management and the ministry identified several areas requiring improvement, including provisions in the company's constitution, compliance with internal policies, internal controls, and integrity and accountability mechanisms.
The ministry said the review must proceed independently and transparently, without undue interference or influence.
It said it would not tolerate attempts to exploit positions, influence or connections to compromise the process.
"The review and related investigations also involve TalentCorp employees and management. All parties must cooperate to ensure the process is conducted fairly and objectively.
"Any further action will be determined by the findings of the review and investigations," it said.
The ministry said TalentCorp's operations and strategic programmes would continue as usual throughout the process, with the agency remaining focused on its national talent development mandate.

Title: Alleged Geng Suria leader, eight others charged as organised crime group members
Article:
SUNGAI PETANI: Nine men were charged in the Sessions Court with being members of an organised crime group known as 'Geng Suria'.
They were Thayalan, 28; A. Tana Balan, 30; Muhamad Rizwan Abd Jalil, 28; G. Sritharan, 39; B. Saranraj, 38; A. Simon, 34; G. Suria Prasad, 30, who is alleged to be the gang leader; A. Suresh, 52; and Kavines, 31.
No pleas were recorded after the charges were read out in Tamil before judges Nabisha Ibrahim and Najwa Che Mat in separate courtrooms, as the case falls under the jurisdiction of the High Court.
The nine were charged with being members of the group at an unnumbered house in Jalan Sekerat, Pekan Lama, here, between December 2024 and April this year.
The charge, under Section 130V(1) of the Penal Code, carries a jail term of up to 20 years upon conviction.
Deputy public prosecutors Yazid Mustaqim Roslan and Mohd Fakhrurrazi Ahmad Salim led the prosecution.
Lawyer S. Sagthiyaraj represented Saranraj and Thayalan, while lawyer Mohammad Naim Kamaruddin represented Sritharan, Simon and Tana Balan. The remaining four accused were unrepresented.
The court denied bail to all nine accused and fixed Nov 17 for mention.

Title: Indonesia channels US$68mil to tackle fires, haze
Article:
JAKARTA: Indonesia has disbursed a second tranche of 1.235 trillion rupiah (about US$68 million) in central government aid to combat forest and land fires, with priority given to healthcare services for affected residents, a senior minister said today.
Human Development and Culture Coordinating Minister Sugiono said the funds would be used to distribute face masks and portable oxygen supplies, establish recovery facilities and treat people suffering from acute respiratory infections.
The aid will finance firefighting equipment, including protective gear, water pumps, hoses and peatland water injectors, as well as personnel deployment and logistical support, Sugiono said.
He said President Prabowo Subianto had instructed authorities to accelerate and coordinate their response to the fires.
About 71,000 personnel have been deployed to combat the blazes, supported by aerial water-bombing and cloud-seeding operations using dry ice, he said.
Forest and land fires, often linked to land clearing and exacerbated by dry weather, have caused widespread haze across parts of Indonesia and neighbouring countries. - BERNAMA

Title: Saudi Aramco orders Dhahran headquarters evacuation as Houthi attacks intensify
Article:
RIYADH:  Saudi state oil company Aramco has told staff to evacuate its headquarters in Dhahran on the Gulf, six people with knowledge of the matter told Reuters on Thursday, as fighting between the world's largest crude exporter and Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis intensifies.
Clashes between the Houthis and a Saudi-led coalition that backs Yemen's internationally recognised government have raged since the group pushed towards Bab el-Mandeb, a shipping ​chokepoint at the Red Sea's mouth.
The instruction to staff to evacuate the building and work remotely follows a wave of Houthi attacks on the kingdom, targeting the company and Saudi airports. The company did not immediately respond to a request for comment on what would be the first evacuation since the start of the Iran war.
It was unclear what the reason for the evacuation was.
The kingdom's benchmark index TASI dropped 2.5 per cent on Thursday following the Aramco news, according to LSEG data. Oil prices rose to their highest since May on Thursday on concern over an escalation of the Middle East conflict and its impact on crude oil supplies from the world's key exporting region.
HOUTHIS SAY THEY TARGETED ARAMCO IN YANBU
Houthi military spokesperson Yahya Saree said in a televised speech that the group had launched attacks on Aramco facilities in the Red Sea city of Yanbu and the Saudi defence ministry in the capital Riyadh. Saudi authorities did not confirm the attack.
The Saudi-led coalition said on Thursday it had intercepted drones over Riyadh and Islam's holy city of Madinah, which is near Yanbu.
The renewed fighting between Saudi Arabia and Houthi militias in recent weeks ended a 2022 UN-brokered truce, which had largely halted cross-border attacks, and opened another front ​in the US-Israeli ⁠war on Iran.
The Houthis caused extensive damage to Aramco's headquarters earlier this month when they struck the building, with fire spreading across several floors.
Saudi Arabia has responded to Houthi attacks with a wave of strikes on missile launcher sites, vowing to protect the kingdom, and says it has intercepted many ballistic missiles fired by the group.
Saree said that Saudi attacks on Yemen have killed and wounded 562 people since mid July, when the Houthis imposed a naval blockade on the kingdom which then drew a warning from the Saudi-led coalition that it ​would respond "firmly."
Separately, he said earlier on Thursday that the group is rescuing a boat carrying 14 Indians that was attacked off Jabal Zuqar island near the strait, one of the territories the group seized in an advance in September.
Saree blamed the attack on Saudi Arabia. Saudi authorities did not respond to a Reuters request for comment.
HOUTHI AIRPORT ATTACKS
A Houthi attack on King Fahd International Airport in Saudi Arabia's eastern oil hub of Dammam near Dhahran on Wednesday evening killed two people, a Saudi citizen and an Indian national, and wounded eight others.
Saudi Arabia's General Authority of Civil Aviation said on Thursday that operations at the airport had resumed and air traffic had returned to normal.
The ​Houthis had warned airlines this month against using Saudi airspace ⁠as they have repeatedly targeted Saudi airports, including Riyadh's international airport and the southern airport of Abha.
Brent crude futures LCOc1 climbed US$3.06, or 2.81 per cent, to US$111.88 a barrel by 1104 GMT on Thursday. They hit US$112.55 a barrel earlier in the session, the highest since May 18.--REUTERS

Title: BNM extends repayment deferments to families of Nepal-China flood victims
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Repayment deferments have been extended to families of victims affected by the recent floods along the Nepal-China border, Bank Negara Malaysia (BNM) said.
In a statement, the central bank said banks and insurance and takaful operators (ITOs) had engaged with the affected families following a meeting between BNM and the victims' next of kin on Oct 12.
"Depending on the specific circumstances of the affected families, banks and ITOs are also considering further assistance, such as waivers of selected fees and charges, protection of customer assets and deposits, and facilitation of insurance/takaful claims.
"Affected families are encouraged to continue engaging directly with their respective banks and ITOs. Should they require further assistance or clarification, they may reach out to their respective financial institution," BNM said.
BNM and the financial industry reiterated their readiness to extend appropriate relief and support to the victims' families, in accordance with applicable laws and regulatory requirements.
It said it would continue to monitor the progress of these efforts.

Title: Jawi appeals RM160,000 damages award to Siti Kasim over wrongful arrest
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: The Federal Territories Islamic Religious Department (Jawi), and 22 others have appealed against a High Court ruling ordering them to pay lawyer and activist Siti Kasim RM160,000 in damages over her wrongful arrest and detention in 2016.
Senior Federal Counsel Ng Siew Wee, representing Jawi, 15 of its officers and seven others, said the appeal centred on three main issues: the element of mens rea (guilty intent) in misfeasance in public office, the allegation of malicious prosecution, and the judge's assessment of witness testimony and records from earlier criminal proceedings.
On the alleged misfeasance in public office, Ng argued that an honest mistake of law by the officers should not automatically be treated as an abuse of power.
"The evidence clearly shows that the motive behind the raid was to enforce the fatwa.
"An honest mistake of law does not constitute misfeasance in public office," she said.
On malicious prosecution, Ng argued that there was insufficient evidence to show that the Jawi enforcement officers who lodged the police report had acted dishonestly to have Siti Kasim charged with obstructing a public servant in the discharge of his duties.
She also argued that the High Court judge had erred in assessing a defendant's testimony and relying on records from an earlier criminal case as substantive evidence in determining liability.
Meanwhile, lawyer A. Saha Deva, representing Siti Kasim, whose full name is Siti Zabedah Kasim, argued that the High Court had properly considered the facts and applied the law.
He said the enforcement officers had proceeded with the raid without properly considering whether they had the legal authority to do so, demonstrating the mens rea required to establish misfeasance in public office.
"They did not care whether they had the authority or not; they proceeded with the raid regardless," he said.
Saha Deva said trial evidence showed that the officers continued with the raid even after Siti Kasim questioned whether their actions had a legal basis.
He also defended the High Court's findings on misfeasance in public office, saying the officers' conduct had to be assessed in light of the evidence as a whole.
A three-member panel chaired by  Datuk Noorin Badaruddin fixed Nov 5 for case management to determine the date for its decision on the appeal.
The other judges on the panel were Datuk Dr Shahnaz Sulaiman and Datuk Meor Hashimi Abdul Hamid.
Siti Kasim filed the civil suit in September 2019 over her alleged wrongful arrest and detention during a raid by Jawi officers at a private fundraising dinner on April 3, 2016. She was subsequently taken to the Dang Wangi district police headquarters.
She claimed the actions amounted to false imprisonment, misfeasance in public office and a violation of her constitutional right to personal liberty.
She maintained that she had been acting in her capacity as a lawyer and had neither obstructed the officers in carrying out their duties nor committed any offence.
Siti Kasim also argued that Jawi had no jurisdiction or investigative powers over offences under the Penal Code.
On July 18, 2025,
High Court Judge Su Tiang Joo
ordered the defendants to pay RM100,000 in exemplary damages, RM60,000 in aggravated damages, and RM100,000 in legal costs to Siti Kassim.
The court held that Siti Kasim had proven on the balance of probabilities that she was wrongfully arrested and falsely imprisoned by two Jawi officers after exiting the ballroom of the hotel where the event was held.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Trump 'behind bars' in Teheran's latest anti-US propaganda stunt
Article:
TEHERAN: Anti-American propaganda is a common sight on the streets of the Iranian capital, but authorities have gone a step further with their latest effort – a life-size jail cell with an actor playing US President Donald Trump languishing inside.
The 3D art installation is proving a hit with locals, who have been stopping to take selfies as well as hurl abuse at Trump, who is accused by Teheran of war crimes during the Middle East war.
Since the beginning of the war that began with American and Israeli strikes in February, the Islamic republic has ramped up propaganda operations, with several pieces of artwork going viral.
In their latest campaign, a prison cell is suspended several stories high in Tajrish Square in an upscale neighbourhood of north Teheran.
Inside is an actor dressed in a dark suit and red tie and wearing a prosthetic mask to look like the US president, as he paces around the cell or clutches its bars.
A screen set up nearby shows messages denouncing US "war crimes."
Some locals were having fun with the installation, with one passerby jokingly telling Trump: "Don't worry, we'll pay your bail and get you out!"
Others used it as a target for their anger, with one teenager shouting: "Trump, this time we're going to kill you!"
Teheran's municipal authorities, which are behind the campaign, said they want to remind the capital's residents of Iran's demands for justice.
Iran has portrayed Trump as a war criminal and called for revenge since the conflict began with US-Israeli strikes that killed the country's supreme leader.
Teheran accuses the US president of deliberately targeting civilian sites, including a school and a wedding ceremony, killing dozens of women and children.
Media outlets close to Iranian authorities have said the latest propaganda installation is designed to operate continuously, day and night, seven days a week.--AFP

Title: TSH Resources says Indonesia operations unaffected by forest fires
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: TSH Resources Bhd said its operations, concessions and other assets in Indonesia had not been affected by recent forest and peatland fires.
In a filing with Bursa Malaysia today, the oil palm company, which operates in Malaysia and Indonesia, said it was responding to a general information request from Singapore Exchange Ltd (SGX) through announcements on Bursa Malaysia Securities Bhd and SGX.
"TSH has not been named or issued any notice by any environmental agency in connection with the recent transboundary haze.
"Under the group's strictly enforced zero-burning policy, the use of fire for any field operations, including land preparation, new planting and replanting, is prohibited across the group," it said.
The policy reflected the group's commitment to preventing land clearing by burning, in compliance with Malaysian and Indonesian laws, it said.
The policy has been incorporated into the group's sustainability policy since May 2009, applies to all group companies and extends to its contractors and suppliers.
"In line with its 'No New Planting on Peat' commitment, the group has not developed any new plantings on peat since the cut-off date of Dec 31, 2015," it said.
The group also has various fire prevention and response measures, spending an estimated average of RM2 million annually on them.
"All of the group's estates in Indonesia are certified under the Indonesian Sustainable Palm Oil (ISPO) scheme, which is subject to regular third-party audits," it added.

Title: Taiwan issues warnings as Typhoon Champi nears
Article:
TAIPEI: A powerful typhoon headed towards Taiwan on Thursday, triggering the cancellation of dozens of flights and prompting warnings for locals to prepare for heavy rain, strong winds and giant waves.
Typhoon Champi is expected to sweep past Taiwan's northeast coast on Friday and Saturday as it moves towards China and Japan, Taiwan's Central Weather Administration (CWA) said.
Champi has maximum sustained wind speeds of nearly 195km per hour, according to the latest update from the Joint Typhoon Warning Center.
It was previously classed as a super typhoon, with reported maximum speeds of nearly 300kph, but has since weakened.
"Everyone is urged to remain vigilant and be prepared for the strong winds and heavy rains brought by the typhoon," Taiwanese President Lai Ching-te said in a Facebook post.
Champi is the latest in a busy Pacific storm season turbo-charged by the El Nino weather phenomenon that has caused unprecedented warming in the equatorial Pacific.
The storm is expected to dump up to 900mm of rain in the mountainous regions of northern and northeastern Taiwan from Thursday to Saturday, and whip up waves more than six metres tall.
Work and classes on Friday have been cancelled in many cities and counties across the island.
More than 23,000 military personnel are on standby to help with rescue efforts. Over 150 domestic and international flights were cancelled for Thursday ahead of the storm.
"Typhoon Champi is expected to have its most significant impact starting all day tomorrow through the first half of Saturday," CWA forecaster Jason Cheng told AFP.
"Currently, the typhoon has a storm radius of 320km... Compared to the previous Typhoon Bavi, Champi's storm area is not as vast," Cheng said.
Millions of people in eastern China also prepared for torrential downpours and flash flooding in the coming days.
China's Ministry of Water Resources initiated a level-four emergency response on Thursday for flooding in Shanghai and the coastal provinces of Jiangsu, Zhejiang and Fujian.
Level four is the lowest in China's emergency response hierarchy.
The ministry warned that Champi could bring "a period of significant rainfall" from Friday to Sunday, with "heavy to torrential downpours" expected in some areas, including "most of Shanghai and eastern Zhejiang."
Japan's two major airlines cancelled more than 110 flights from Thursday to Saturday.
The United Nations said Wednesday that the El Nino system gripping the planet is heading off the charts, and that countries should take urgent action to prepare for the worst.
El Nino is expected to peak in December, but the human impact is set to last into 2027 and beyond.
The warming phase of a natural climate cycle, El Nino temporarily raises sea temperatures in the tropical Pacific, triggering changes in weather that can increase the risk of drought and flooding, and exacerbate human-caused global warming.--AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Evergrande's US$46bil debt nightmare yields just 1pct recovery
Article:
HONG KONG: China Evergrande Group's liquidators have recovered US$435.9 million from asset sales and loan recoveries so far, highlighting the challenge of repaying creditors with claims of about US$46 billion against the developer.
In their second progress report since a Hong Kong court ordered Evergrande's liquidation in January 2024, the liquidators, Edward Middleton and Tiffany Wong of Alvarez & Marsal, said on Thursday they aimed to make a first interim dividend payment to creditors in the first half of 2027, although the amount has yet to be determined.
Evergrande, once China's top property developer, defaulted on most of its roughly US$300 billion in liabilities and became a symbol of the property crisis that has weighed on the world's second-largest economy.
The liquidators said they had raised the US$435.9 million through the sale of assets including aircraft, artwork and club memberships, as well as the settlement of loan receivables.
They said 96 of the 107 artworks found at Evergrande's Hong Kong headquarters had been sold for US$28.8 million at a loss. The collection included works by Picasso, Monet and Warhol, as well as sculptures by Moore and Hepworth.
Other assets being sold include a private jet expected to fetch about US$12 million in the fourth quarter. The liquidators are also seeking a US$2 million refund from a US university for part of a donation made in 2020.
The liquidators have taken control of more than 100 Evergrande subsidiaries across multiple jurisdictions, but said prospects for recovering assets held by mainland Chinese subsidiaries were "considered remote."
In August, Evergrande founder Hui Ka Yan, 67, was sentenced to life imprisonment by a Chinese court, which also ordered the confiscation of his personal assets.
Industry experts say Evergrande's liquidation could take more than a decade to complete given the scale and complexity of the group.--REUTERS

Title: 14 cases of fallen trees reported across Seberang Prai after heavy rain
Article:
BUTTERWORTH: Fourteen fallen tree incidents were reported in various parts on mainland Penang, with cleanup operations ongoing at several locations.
The Seberang Prai City Council (MBSP) said works to clear fallen trees and other debris were being carried out to ensure public safety and minimise disruption to road users and residents.
"Cleanup operations at some locations have been completed, while work at others are ongoing," it said in a statement on its Facebook page.
Heavy rain was reported in several parts of the mainland yesterday, resulting in flash floods.
MBSP said the efforts were aimed at restoring affected areas, ensuring smooth traffic flow and safeguarding the well-being of residents.
The city council advised the public to exercise caution when travelling through areas where cleanup operations were still underway and to cooperate with personnel on the ground.
"Public safety and the comfort and well-being of Seberang Prai residents remain our priority," it added.

Title: Zetrix AI to hold sukukholders' meeting on covenant breach
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Zetrix AI Bhd will hold a meeting with sukukholders on Friday to discuss a proposed resolution to its covenant breach involving the shareholding of a substantial shareholder.
In a filing with Bursa Malaysia tonight, the company said no payment default had occurred as at Thursday.
"The sukuk trustee, Pacific Trustee Bhd, will convene a meeting with all the sukuk holders on Oct 23 to discuss the matter with a proposed resolution to address the cause of the breach, in relation to the shareholding of the substantial shareholder.
"The meeting aims to facilitate constructive discussions and gather feedback from the sukuk holders on the proposed resolution," it said in the filing.
The company added that the engagement will serve as a basis for formulating and formalising an appropriate arrangement that is mutually acceptable to the relevant parties.
"The company is committed to meet its sukuk repayment obligations in line with the agreed schedule and continues to take the necessary steps to support its financial commitments.
"In the meantime, the company will continue to engage with the sukuk trustee to address the matter," it said.
Zetrix AI Bhd faces a potential covenant breach under its RM2 billion sukuk Wakalah after its managing director Wong Thean Soon ceased to be the company's single largest shareholder following forced share sales by banks.
In a filing with Bursa Malaysia on Oct 16,  the company said Wong's combined direct and indirect shareholding fell to 1.895 per cent as of Oct 15 following the forced sale of his shares by banks.
The sukuk requires Wong to remain the company's single largest shareholder, directly or indirectly.

Title: Malaysia gets Southeast Asia's only AMG One service hub
Article:
MERCEDES-Benz Malaysia has invested RM2.2 million in a specialised service hub for the Mercedes-AMG One hypercar, making the nation the only location in Southeast Asia equipped to service the Formula 1-derived model.
Located at Hap Seng Star's Bukit Tinggi facility, the hub joins a limited global network serving owners of the road-legal hypercar, of which only 275 units were produced worldwide.
The facility will support owners across Southeast Asia, complementing an existing service hub in Japan.
It is equipped with specialised high-voltage tools, vehicle-specific diagnostic systems and controlled storage and working conditions to meet the model's technical requirements.
The Malaysia-based technicians have undergone specialised training and received Mercedes-AMG certification to carry out approved diagnostic, maintenance and servicing procedures.
The team will also coordinate directly with Mercedes-AMG specialists in Affalterbach, Germany for technical support.
The Mercedes-AMG One combines a 1.6-litre V6 turbocharged engine with four electric motors, producing a total system output of more than 1,063 horsepower.
Its hybrid powertrain draws directly on F1 technology, making servicing more complex than that of conventional performance cars.
Mercedes-Benz Malaysia chief executive officer Martin Schulz said the facility builds on Malaysia's existing role in supporting the company's regional operations.
The hub's location also provides access to Mercedes-Benz Parts Logistics Asia Pacific's operations in Malaysia, which the company said would help streamline parts distribution and reduce delays in maintenance and repairs.
Other services include regional technical support, dedicated liaison officers for international customers and digital systems for diagnostic reporting and service updates.
The investment comes as Malaysia seeks to expand its high-value services sector under the 13th Malaysia Plan for 2026 to 2030.
The facility adds a specialised automotive service capability to the country's existing logistics and aftersales operations.
Hap Seng Star, which operates the Bukit Tinggi facility, will provide servicing for AMG One owners from Malaysia and other regional markets.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Court ruling strengthens PN's resolve ahead of Melaka polls, says Hamzah
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The High Court's decision to stay Perikatan Nasional's suspension and deregistration has strengthened the coalition's resolve ahead of the Melaka election.
Parti Wawasan Negara (Wawasan) president Datuk Seri Hamzah Zainudin said the decision also offered renewed hope for PN to participate in the country's democratic process in a healthy and fair manner.
"Power is not a licence to act as one pleases. The law must not be used as a tool to suppress those with differing views.
"Today's positive decision will further strengthen PN's resolve to consolidate its position, offer the people the best policies and services, and translate these efforts into public support in the upcoming Melaka election," he said in a statement.
Earlier, High Court judge Datuk Azizan Md Arshad allowed PN's application to
stay its suspension
and subsequent deregistration by the Registrar of Societies (RoS).
The decision comes just nine days before nomination day for the Melaka election, paving the way for the coalition to resume its  political activities and preparations to contest under its own name and symbol.
"Wawasan welcomes the High Court's decision to stay the RoS notice concerning the revocation of PN's registration, allowing the coalition to use its logo in the upcoming Melaka state election.
"Today's decision is in line with the late Sultan Azlan Shah's judgment in the 1979 case of Director of Lands and Mines, Federal Territory v Sri Lempah Enterprise Sdn Bhd, which stated that 'every power must have legal limits, otherwise it will lead to dictatorial rule'," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Thailand to tighten cannabis controls, propose tougher penalties
Article:
BANGKOK: Thailand plans to tighten cannabis regulations and propose tougher penalties for violations as part of broader efforts to strengthen drug prevention and enforcement.
Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul said the proposed amendments to the Narcotics Act concerning cannabis were discussed at the third meeting of the Office of the Narcotics Control Board (ONCB) this year on Thursday.
"Drug policies must be guided by scientific evidence, facts and the public interest," he said in a statement published on the Royal Thai Government website.
He said the government would maintain a clear distinction between medical cannabis use and recreational consumption.
The Ministry of Public Health and relevant agencies had also been directed to inspect licensed establishments and take legal action against operators who breach their licence conditions, including possible revocation, he said.
Anutin said the meeting also discussed amendments to drug laws to improve enforcement against drug possession, including small-quantity offences, while ensuring that treatment and rehabilitation were appropriately considered alongside legal action.
Anutin said he had also instructed the Customs Department to step up inspections, intelligence gathering and random checks to prevent the illegal export of goods, particularly those potentially linked to narcotics.
"Exports of cannabis stems, leaves and flower buds must strictly comply with Thai law, while cannabidiol (CBD) extracts could be exported subject to licensing requirements and regulations set by the Food and Drug Administration (FDA)," he said.
Thailand decriminalised cannabis in 2022, but amid concerns about recreational use and the rapid expansion of cannabis-related businesses, the government has since moved to tighten regulations.
On Sept 22, the Thai cabinet approved a draft Cannabis and Hemp Act to restrict cannabis strictly to medical use and phase out the recreational market.
Separately, on security in Thailand's southern border provinces, Anutin said the National Security Council had convened relevant security, intelligence and administrative agencies to formulate a unified operational strategy.
"The aim is to ensure that all agencies have a common understanding and work together under the same strategic plan in a unified manner," he said.
He added that security agencies had been instructed to closely monitor developments, strengthen surveillance and coordinate intelligence to prevent further escalation and safeguard public order and residents' safety. — BERNAMA
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Ramanan questions Rafizi's claims over alleged RM9.5mil payment to corporate mafia
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: PKR vice-president Datuk Seri R. Ramanan has questioned Datuk Seri Rafizi Ramli's claims that he received RM9.5 million from businessman Victor Chin to resolve a corporate mafia issue.
Ramanan said it had been seven months since the allegation was made, but Rafizi had yet to present any evidence.
He also criticised Rafizi for allegedly making unsubstantiated statements and subsequently seeking public donations to cover legal costs after losing court cases.
"I have not taken any action so far. After losing in court, he collects donations from the public, asking them to help him avoid bankruptcy.
"So, if you want me to sue him, who am I suing? Who would I be burdening? I would be burdening the public if I sued him," he said on the sidelines of the Human Resources Ministry staff appreciation ceremony.
Ramanan was responding to Rafizi's remarks two days ago that he had yet to receive a letter of demand from Ramanan over the alleged RM9.5 million payment.
Ramanan said the main issue was not whether legal action would be taken, but whether Rafizi could substantiate his allegations.
"Does he have even one piece of evidence? Where is it? That is why I called him a serial liar.
"He makes claims without evidence or facts, then asks the public to defend him. Who does that?" he said.
Ramanan also said he had served the public without drawing a salary or other allowances.
"I am not involved in dirty politics like Rafizi.
"I did not want to respond to this issue, but as a party vice-president, I have to, especially since the party president has also addressed it," he said.

Title: Fires rage, haze spreads as Indonesians pray for rain
Article:
SURABAYA: Indonesian schoolchildren prayed for rain on Thursday as another firefighter lost his life battling drought-fuelled blazes consuming forests and peatlands and blanketing parts of Southeast Asia in a sickening haze.
Wildfires have burned more than 1.9 million hectares in the nine months to September, according to deforestation monitor Nusantara Atlas – a figure the government has not confirmed or denied.
The resulting haze has sickened hundreds of thousands in Indonesia and reached as far as Malaysia, Singapore and East Timor.
In East Java, where fires have ravaged several regencies and conservation areas including Mount Bromo and the Baluran National Park, the governor urged communities to come together to "pray for rain."
"Many areas are experiencing drought, including fires and so on... Religion offers a way to solve the problem of drought," teacher Mohamad Jatim told AFP of prayers organised at his school in Surabaya, the capital of East Java.
"As people of faith, we are of course optimistic."
In Malang, also in the province, some 250 pupils bowed in prayer with their teachers at a vocational high school.
"We hope that this... will bring rain soon," said headmaster Lusia Andriani.
"There have... been many cases of acute respiratory infections in Indonesia, partly because the rain has not fallen for a prolonged period."
- FIREFIGHTER KILLED -
Indonesia experiences fires every dry season, but this year's blazes have been particularly severe, making hundreds of thousands of people ill.
The haze has prompted school closures in Malaysia and East Timor, and has drifted into Singapore and as far afield as the Philippines.
Five firefighters died in East Java last week after they were overwhelmed by smoke and flames in the Bromo Tengger Semeru National Park.
Another firefighter died on Wednesday in South Kalimantan on Indonesia's part of Borneo island.
The Mahatir Mohammad Zain Foundation, a disaster relief NGO, said the 51-year-old volunteer passed away after falling ill with chest tightness while helping fight a fire in the Barito Kuala Regency.
His death was "a reminder of the risks volunteers face in handling forest and land fires", said the foundation.
The crisis has sparked protests against the government's perceived slow response, as well as a court case against President Prabowo Subianto and other officials in West Kalimantan.
In the capital Jakarta, a dozen demonstrators gathered outside the Chinese embassy on Thursday demanding importers of Indonesian palm oil, mining and forestry products stand in "solidarity" with Indonesia.
Back in Malang, resident Ahmad Saifuddin joined others in praying for divine intervention.
"For the past few days, I have been wondering why almost everyone is trying to solve these disasters using logic. Why don't we try seeking a solution from the heavens instead?" he told AFP.--AFP

Title: Marine & General cautiously bullish about upstream outlook
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Marine & General Bhd maintains a cautiously optimistic outlook for its upstream division, underpinned by long-term contracts for its 60-metre anchor handling tug supply (AHTS) vessels.
The outlook is also supported by an expected gradual recovery in Malaysia's exploration and development activities between 2026 and 2028.
Following its 29th annual general meeting (AGM) held earlier today, the company said the ageing regional offshore support vessel (OSV) fleet.
This was due to limited investment in new vessels during the prolonged downturn in offshore services, is also expected to support a relatively stable market balance.
"Nevertheless, near-term conditions remain competitive, as normalisation in domestic charter rates and more competitive tendering may affect margins," it said in a statement.
The division also faces industry-wide challenges from the energy transition, rising drilling and operating costs, and increasing environmental, social and governance compliance requirements.
"Our focus will continue to be on operational reliability, cost management, vessel availability and fleet optimisation to support charter performance and resilience."
For the downstream division, the company said the Malaysian tanker market is expected to remain stable in the near term, supported by consistent downstream activity and refined
product distribution.
Overall, the group maintains a neutral outlook for the next financial year.
"This reflects the support from long-term contracts for its 60-metre AHTS vessels and the expected gradual increase in exploration and development activities in Malaysia, balanced against prevailing market conditions, global economic uncertainties and geopolitical risks.
"The group will continue to manage its operations and capital resources prudently, with operational decisions guided by market developments and economic conditions."
Eight ordinary resolutions were presented for consideration by the company's shareholders at the AGM. All resolutions were duly passed by the shareholders.

Title: Ringgit ends easier against greenback, major currencies ahead of FOMC meeting
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR:  The ringgit closed lower against the greenback and other major currencies on Thursday as investors remained cautious ahead of next week's two-day US Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting.
This came amid a decline in US Treasury yields and the US Dollar Index (DXY).
At 6pm, the ringgit eased to 4.0815/0850 against the greenback from Wednesday's close of 4.0790/0825.
Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said market participants' reassessment of next week's FOMC decision drove movements in the US DXY, with traders likely to focus on the accompanying FOMC statement for clues on a possible rate hike in December.
"In that sense, support for the DXY is still visible, and the US dollar-ringgit pair could continue to trade within a narrow range," he said.
At the close, the ringgit traded lower against a basket of major currencies.
It decreased versus the Japanese yen to 2.6035/6057 from 2.5790/5814 at Wednesday's close; it declined against the British pound to 5.4659/4706 from 5.4642/4689, and it inched down vis-a-vis the euro to 4.5790/5830 from 4.5770/5810.
The ringgit performed mostly higher against its Asean peers.
It gained versus the Thai baht to 12.0973/1120 from 12.1287/1434 at yesterday's close, appreciated against the Indonesian rupiah to 225.9/226.3 from 226.2/226.7 and strengthened vis-a-vis the Philippine peso to 6.42/6.43 from 6.44/6.45.
The ringgit eased against the Singapore dollar to 3.1959/1992 from 3.1917/1947 at Wednesday's close.

Title: Suspect in MCBA officer's murder remanded for another seven days
Article:
SEREMBAN: The man suspected of murdering his wife, a Malaysian Border Control and Protection Agency (MCBA) officer, at their home on Oct 15 has been remanded for another seven days.
Negri Sembilan police chief Datuk Alzafny Ahmad said the suspect's initial remand, which began on Oct 16, expired today.
"The initial remand expired today. Police applied for an extension at the Seremban magistrate's court, which granted another seven days until Oct 29," he said when contacted.
The suspect had reportedly
surrendered himself
at the Bandar Baru Salak Tinggi police station in Sepang, Selangor, after his wife was found murdered at a government quarters unit along Jalan Kuarters KLIA, Nilai.
He was recently released from prison after serving time for a drug-related offence and was arrested before being remanded from Oct 16.
A post-mortem found that the 35-year-old woman died from pressure on her neck. Stab wounds were also found on her abdomen and cheek.
The case was being investigated under Section 302 of the Penal Code for murder.

Title: Gold futures end lower, in line with US Commodity Exchange losses

Title: Petronas expands global two-wheeler reach through UM Motorcycles pact
Article:
PETRONAS Lubricants International (PLI) has partnered UM Motorcycles to supply motorcycle lubricants across selected markets in Asia Pacific, Europe, Africa and Latin America, expanding its global reach in the two-wheeler segment.
Under the agreement, PLI will supply selected products from its Petronas Sprinta range to UM Motorcycles' distributors and aftersales dealer networks, with the initial rollout beginning in Asia this month.
The lubricants, featuring PLI's UltraFlex technology, are designed to enhance engine responsiveness, protect critical components and improve reliability and longevity.
The technology is intended to provide protection across the engine, clutch and gears, including during cold starts, stop-start traffic and demanding road conditions.
The partnership will also cover dealer development, technical training and coordinated marketing activities.
It is aimed at strengthening aftersales support and customer engagement across UM Motorcycles' international network.
PLI said the collaboration would provide opportunities to expand its presence through UM Motorcycles' distribution footprint, while participating distributors and dealers could draw on its lubricant expertise to improve service quality and aftersales reliability.
The Petronas Sprinta range will be introduced progressively across UM Motorcycles' participating distributor and dealer networks, with the first batch scheduled to reach outlets this month.
Following the initial launch in Asia, the rollout will extend to Europe, the Middle East and Africa before reaching the Americas.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Queen donates 376,000 face masks to KL, Putrajaya schoolchildren
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Her Majesty Raja Zarith Sofiah, Queen of Malaysia, has donated 376,000 face masks to schoolchildren in Kuala Lumpur and Putrajaya to help protect them from the haze.
According to a post on Sultan Ibrahim Sultan Iskandar's official Facebook page, the masks will be distributed to students in 289 schools in Kuala Lumpur and 28 schools in Putrajaya, with priority given to those from low-income families.
The masks were handed over by Comptroller of the Royal Household Tan Sri Dr Azmi Rohani to the principals and headmasters of the respective schools at the Federal Territory of Kuala Lumpur Education Department.
The donation was made through Yayasan Raja Zarith Sofiah Negeri Johor, in collaboration with the Jeffrey Cheah Foundation and Wangsa Ultima Sdn Bhd.
Also present were Grand Chamberlain of the Royal Household Datuk Azuan Effendy Zairakithnaini, Yayasan Raja Zarith Sofiah Negeri Johor chief executive officer Hishamuddin Abdul Rahim, and Education Ministry Deputy Director (Student Affairs Management) Hirudin Mohit.
Previously, the Queen donated 500,000 face masks to students in Johor and nearly 300,000 masks to frontline personnel in the state, including members of the Malaysia Border Control and Protection Agency and the police.
She also donated 200,000 face masks to Malaysian motorcyclists commuting to work in Singapore amid the haze affecting Johor.
