Title: Telegram-based prostitution, human trafficking syndicate raking in RM5.4mil a year busted
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: An organised crime group which have raked in up to RM5.4 million a year from prostitution and human trafficking used a Telegram channel to advertise its services, with an estimated 100 customers daily.
Federal Criminal Investigation Department director Datuk M Kumar said the group, known as Geng Yunaa, operated through the 'KLSELANGORFL' channel, offering an estimated 20 to 30 sex workers a day.
Customers were charged between RM200 and RM350, payable in cash, through Touch 'n Go transfers or banking QR codes.
"The group is believed to have served about 100 customers a day, collecting RM150 from each customer, while the remainder was paid to the sex workers.
"Based on this estimate, the group could generate RM15,000 a day," he said in a statement.
Police have since crippled the group in Op Angel, conducted across the Klang Valley from Sept 24 to 26.
Kumar said the group, comprising 10 members, had been active since early 2024 and recruited local teenagers, foreigners and underage children for sexual exploitation through prostitution in Selangor and Kuala Lumpur.
Acting on intelligence, police arrested seven suspects aged between 18 and 44, including the group's 30-year-old leader.
"All the suspects are being detained under the Security Offences (Special Measures) Act 2012 (Sosma) until Oct 23.
"Two other group members are being held at Kajang Prison and Henry Gurney School in Melaka over child trafficking and prostitution offences," he said.
Kumar said police were also tracking another member who remained at large.
He expressed serious concern over the exploitation of minors, saying the group's activities posed a threat to vulnerable individuals and social well-being.
"Geng Yunaa's activities are not merely prostitution offences, but also constitute serious sexual exploitation of vulnerable groups, particularly children, for substantial financial gain," he said.
During the operation, police seized 14 mobile phones, 33 boxes of condoms, six boxes of contraceptive medication, towels and lubricant gel.
Checks also found that several suspects had previous criminal records involving prostitution, drug trafficking, human trafficking and fraud.
Kumar said the operation had enabled police to solve 17 prostitution and child trafficking cases in Selangor.
He said nine group members would be brought before the Petaling Jaya Sessions Court tomorrow (Oct 23) and charged under Section 130V(1) of the Penal Code for being members of an organised crime group.
The offence carries a prison term of between five and 20 years upon conviction.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Stolen luxury goods, devices, put up for sale after Paris looting [WATCH]
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Luxury goods looted from high-end boutiques in Paris are being resold on the streets, with videos showing designer handbags, watches and tech products from ransacked stores circulating online amid the unrest in France.
Clips shared on social media showed designer merchandise, including items from Hermès, Dior and Louis Vuitton, among others, laid out on the ground for sale, while some looters were seen flaunting their haul online.
Footage from the haul also drew reactions from social media users, with some questioning whether the looters could be traced through the stolen tech devices.
"Do they know they can be tracked?" user geezy101_ commented.
"Stealing smart electronics is the most stupid thing one can do," said another user.
"All of those devices they stole are already blocked and out of use, they are useless," another user commented.
[[nid:1561478]]
Meanwhile, some of the stolen goods have surfaced on Vinted, a second-hand fashion resale platform, prompting the company to identify and remove listings suspected of containing stolen merchandise.
France's digital minister has also urged resale platforms to remove listings for stolen items and summoned representatives of companies, including Vinted and eBay, to discuss further action.
The scale of the damage was also evident on Avenue Montaigne, a luxury shopping street in Paris, where windows at Louis Vuitton and Jil Sander stores were smashed, while a Celine boutique was stripped bare, Le Monde reported.
Beyond luxury boutiques, grocery stores and eateries operated by local sellers were also targeted, according to the circulating clips, leaving shop owners to grapple with losses and damage to their businesses.
The unrest, reportedly fuelled by anger over student welfare, deteriorating public services and the rising cost of living, has triggered widespread violence and looting.
Closer to home, the Foreign Ministry said on Oct 18 that
no Malaysians had been reported involved
in or affected by the unrest, after advising Malaysians in France to report their whereabouts to the Malaysian embassy.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: High Court stay gives PN room to prepare for Melaka election
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Perikatan Nasional will focus on strengthening its preparations for the Melaka election after the High Court today stayed the Registrar of Societies Malaysia's (RoS) action to cancel the coalition's registration.
Its chairman, Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Samsuri Mokhtar said PN was grateful for the decision and maintained that it was on the right track in defending its rights through legal channels.
He said efforts by those seeking to "erase" PN would not weaken the coalition's resolve, adding that it would remain steadfast and continue its struggle.
"Thank you to everyone for their prayers, support and patience, as well as to the legal team for their tireless efforts.
"We will continue to respect the ongoing legal process and firmly defend our rights.
"Now, the entire machinery must focus fully on the Melaka election. Strengthen preparations, foster closer cooperation and offer the best for the people. We will keep moving forward," he said in a statement here today.
The High Court
allowed PN's application to stay the implementation of the RoS
action pending the full disposal of the substantive judicial review proceedings.
Judge Datuk Azizan Md Arshad made the decision after finding that exceptional circumstances justified the stay, particularly given the potential harm to the applicant's political activities and participation in the country's electoral system.
It was previously reported that RoS had confirmed the cancellation of PN's registration after finding that the coalition's explanations had failed to refute the grounds for cancellation stated in an earlier notice.
RoS said the decision was made under subparagraph 13(1)(c)(iv) of the Societies Act 1966 after reviewing all documents and representations submitted by PN on Oct 12.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Police bust alleged sex trafficking syndicate exploiting children, generating RM450,000 monthly
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 22 — Police have crippled ‘Geng Yunaa’, believed to be involved in 17 cases of child prostitution and trafficking for sexual exploitation, following ‘Ops Angel’ in the Klang Valley from Sept 24 to 26.
Bukit Aman Criminal Investigation Department director Datuk M. Kumar said seven individuals, aged between 18 and 44, were detained under the Security Offences (Special Measures) Act 2012 (SOSMA) until tomorrow.
He said two other group members were already being held at Kajang Prison and Henry Gurney School in Melaka for offences related to child trafficking and prostitution.
“The group carried out sexual exploitation through prostitution by recruiting local teenagers, foreign nationals and underage children, who were exploited and made victims of prostitution in Selangor and Kuala Lumpur.
“To attract customers, the group used the Telegram application to promote prostitution services, with an estimated 20 to 30 sex workers operating daily,” he said in a statement today.
Kumar said customers were charged between RM200 and RM350, depending on the package and service location. Payments were believed to have been made in cash or through Touch ‘n Go or banking QR codes to prostitution agents linked to the group.
He said the group was believed to have served about 100 customers daily, collecting RM150 from each customer, while the remainder was paid to the individuals being exploited.
Based on these estimates, the group could generate RM15,000 a day, or RM450,000 a month, equivalent to RM5.4 million a year if the activity continued at the same rate.
“This activity is deeply concerning because it not only involves trafficking in human beings for profit but also exploits children, who should be protected from abuse and sexual exploitation.
“More worryingly, the sexual exploitation of underage children can leave long-lasting psychological trauma, damage their emotional, moral and social development, and affect their future,” he said.
Kumar said Geng Yunaa, which had been active since early 2024, comprised 10 members aged between 18 and 44 and was led by a 30-year-old local man.
During the operation, police also seized various items believed to be linked to prostitution activities, including 14 mobile phones, six boxes of contraceptive medication, towels and lubricating gel.
“Checks found that several of those arrested had previous records for various offences, including prostitution, human trafficking, drug distribution and fraud.
“We have also identified another group member who remains at large, and efforts to track down the suspect are ongoing,” he said.
Kumar said the investigation papers had been referred to the Serious Crimes Unit of the Attorney-General’s Chambers, which had agreed that nine members of the group be charged under Section 130V(1) of the Penal Code at the Petaling Jaya Sessions Court tomorrow. — Bernama

Title: Viral Porsche road bully jailed five days, fined RM10,000 for dangerous driving
Article:
PETALING JAYA, Oct 22 — A Porsche Cayenne driver was sentenced to five days in prison and fined RM10,000 by the Magistrate’s Court here today after pleading guilty to dangerous driving of the luxury car on a highway near Bandar Kinrara, which had gone viral on social media.
Magistrate Nur Natasya Mohtaruddin, who handed down the sentence against Woo Hong Jiang, 56, ordered the man to serve his prison term starting today, alongside a five-year disqualification of his driving license and six months’ imprisonment if he fails to pay the fine.
The man, who was unrepresented by a lawyer, was charged with driving the vehicle in a manner dangerous to himself and other road users along the Puchong Bypass heading towards Bukit Jalil, Serdang, at 2:14 pm on October 18.
The charge was brought under Section 42(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987 (Act 333), which provides for a maximum imprisonment of five years and a fine ranging from RM5,000 to RM15,000.
Deputy Public Prosecutor Adriana Maisarah Mohd Farid requested a heavy sentence, taking into account that dashboard camera (dashcam) footage showed the accused was a road bully who drove dangerously and whose actions could have caused an accident, noting also that the case had gone viral.
“The accused deserves a high fine and a prison term exceeding the minimum period to serve as a lesson to him and the public not to repeat the same offence,” she said. — Bernama

Title: MCMC warns against sharing Kuching school violence footage involving teen, cautions of legal action
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Oct 22 — The Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) urges individuals who have uploaded or shared video footage of an incident involving a dangerous weapon at a school in Kuching, Sarawak, to immediately delete the content.
In a statement today, MCMC emphasised that the dissemination of footage depicting acts of violence particularly involving children not only compromises the privacy and dignity of those involved but also negatively impacts the emotional well-being of the individuals and their families.
The Commission further cautioned that disclosing the identities of children may constitute a violation of Section 15 of the Child Act 2001 (Act 611).
“The dissemination of such content may also be subject to action under Section 233 of the Communications and Multimedia Act 1998 (Act 588), should it contravene the provisions of the law,” the statement read.
MCMC said it is currently collaborating with social media platform providers to curb the spread of the footage, which includes taking steps to remove the relevant content.
Accordingly, MCMC advises the public, including media practitioners, to refrain from uploading, sharing, or further circulating the video of the incident.
“The public is also reminded not to recirculate such content, in order to protect the privacy of the child involved and to avoid interfering with the authorities’ investigation,” the statement added. — Bernama

Title: Samsuri rallies Perikatan machinery for Melaka polls after court freezes RoS deregistration
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 22 — Perikatan Nasional (PN) chairman Datuk Seri Ahmad Samsuri Mokhtar has welcomed a High Court ruling granting an interim stay against the Registrar of Societies’ (RoS) decision to deregister the coalition, saying it will now direct its full electoral machinery towards the Melaka state election.
In a statement today, Ahmad Samsuri said that PN was “on the right path in defending our rights through legal channels” and maintained that political adversaries seeking to “erase” the coalition would fail to undermine its resolve.
“PN remains steadfast, and this struggle will continue,” he said, offering gratitude to supporters for their prayers and commending the coalition’s legal team for securing the urgent court intervention.
Earlier today, High Court Judge Datuk Azizan Md Arshad allowed PN’s leave application to stay the RoS order revoking the coalition’s corporate registration pending the final disposal of its substantive judicial review challenge.
The court concurrently froze the enforcement of an accompanying RoS directive that had ordered the immediate suspension of all PN operations nationwide.
The interim stay removes a legal cloud hovering over the coalition, allowing PN to operate unhindered as an approved political entity and field candidates under its official logo for the Melaka state election set for Nov 14.
With the legal hurdle cleared, Ahmad Samsuri instructed the coalition’s grassroots wings to pivot immediately from courtroom battles to the ballot box, rallying party workers to “strengthen preparations, foster closer cooperation and present the best offerings to the people.”
“We shall continue to move forward,” he said.

Title: Anthony Loke backs local transport apps with open data on train schedules, passenger numbers
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 22 — Local application developers can leverage open public transport data to help commuters plan their journeys more conveniently, Transport Minister Anthony Loke said.
He said the Transport Ministry (MoT) had adopted an open data policy several years ago, allowing interested parties to access the information to develop public transport applications.
“Public transport data has been made available for several years, and it can be accessed by anyone interested in developing applications,” he told reporters after launching the Masjid Jamek LRT Station beautification project here today.
Loke was responding to a question on the ministry’s support for the development of a local application ecosystem, particularly in terms of access to data.
He said the ministry encouraged the development of local applications that could make public transport more convenient for the public.
“Data under the ministry’s purview mainly relates to public transport, while road-related data involves other agencies, including the Works Ministry and the Public Works Department.
“Prasarana Malaysia Berhad (Prasarana) has made various datasets available to the public, covering daily passenger numbers, train frequency and service schedules,” he said.
At the event, Loke launched Phase Three of the Masjid Jamek LRT Station beautification project, which involves a RM5 million investment by Prasarana to improve commuter comfort and the station environment.
Also present were Kuala Lumpur Mayor Datuk Seri Fadlun Mak Ujud, Prasarana acting president and group chief executive officer Dr Prodyut Dutt, and Think City managing director Datuk Hamdan Abdul Majeed.
Yesterday, the government decided to prohibit all civil servants from using the Waze navigation application to protect government information and users’ personal data from the risk of misuse by the Israeli regime.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the decision took into account Waze Mobile Ltd’s status as a data controller for users, with the company incorporated and operating under Israeli law. — Bernama

Title: MACC chief urges MCMC staff to expose misconduct and reject abuse of power
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Oct 22 — Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) staff have been urged to uphold integrity and good governance to preserve public trust in the country’s communications institution.
Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) Chief Commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman said MCMC staff should have the courage to report any abuse of power or unlawful instructions through official channels.
“Have the courage to stand up for what is right and report any misconduct. Wrongdoing must never be covered up,” he said in his address at the MCMC 2026 Integrity and Audit Month closing ceremony, details of which were shared on the MACC’s Facebook page today.
Abd Halim said MCMC’s integrity programmes showed that both its senior management and staff were committed to strengthening accountability.
He said integrity went beyond compliance with written rules and audit requirements, stemming instead from personal values and principles, especially when honesty and trustworthiness were tested.
“Everyone must uphold the trust placed in them, regardless of their rank or position, and authority must not be treated as a privilege.
“Every decision involving licensing, enforcement, procurement, human resource management and industrial relations must be made transparently,” he said.
The MCMC 2026 Integrity and Audit Month closing ceremony, themed “Empowering Integrity, Strengthening Governance”, was held at the MCMC Auditorium in Cyberjaya today.
Also present were Communications Ministry secretary-general and MCMC Audit and Risk Committee member Datuk Abdul Halim Hamzah; MCMC chairman Tan Sri Mohamad Salim Fateh Din; and MCMC commissioner and Audit and Risk Committee chairman Prof Dr Mohamad Salmi Mohd Sohod.
Others in attendance included MCMC commissioner General (Rtd) Tan Sri Zulkifeli Mohd Zin, MCMC managing director Abdul Karim Fakir Ali and Malaysian Anti-Corruption Academy senior director Datuk Mohamad Zamri Zainul Abidin.
Meanwhile, Mohamad Salmi said MCMC remained committed to curbing corruption and ensuring that accountable governance systems were consistently implemented.
“MCMC strives to ensure that the benefits of every fund it manages are returned to the people in a transparent and orderly manner,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Two men in viral Bukit Antarabangsa police chase charged with dangerous driving, drugs and weapons offences
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 22 — Two men who went viral on social media after crashing into public vehicles while attempting to evade police in Bukit Antarabangsa were charged in three separate courts in Ampang today on various offences, including obstructing civil servants, possessing dangerous weapons and drugs.
Private driver Muhammad Putra Zulfaiz Zaidi, 32, and mechanic Mohamad Danial Haiqal Kamal Arifin, 21, pleaded not guilty to all charges read before Sessions Court Judge Norshila Kamarudin and Magistrates Siti Nur Ain Ariffin and Tiong Wen Wen.
Before Judge Norshila Kamarudin, the two friends were jointly charged with possessing dangerous weapons in a public place, namely a machete and a sickle, at Jalan Wangsa 5, Bukit Antarabangsa, at 11 am on Oct 11.
The charge is framed under Section 6(1) of the Corrosive and Explosive Substances and Offensive Weapons Act 1958, read together with Section 34 of the Penal Code, which provides for imprisonment between five and 10 years, as well as caning.
Meanwhile, before Magistrate Siti Nur Ain, the duo faced two charges of obstructing police duties under Section 186 of the Penal Code, read together with Section 34 of the Penal Code, which carries imprisonment of up to two years or a fine of up to RM10,000, or both.
On the first charge, both men are accused of obstructing Cpl Muhammad Azfar Abdul Rahman and Lance Cpl Muhammad Yashar Hassan by fleeing in an Isuzu D-Max four-wheel-drive at Jalan Wangsa 5 at 11 am on Oct 11. The second charge involves Cpl Mohamad Syisyi Pauzi at Jalan Wangsa 1 at 5.30 am on Oct 10.
In the same court, Muhammad Putra Zulfaiz was charged individually with driving the four-wheel-drive with a false registration number under the Road Transport Act 1987.
He was also charged with consuming amphetamine and methamphetamine at the Ampang Jaya District Police Headquarters’ Narcotics Criminal Investigation Division office at 10.45 pm on Oct 11, under Section 15(1)(a) of the Dangerous Drugs Act 1952.
Before Magistrate Tiong, they were jointly charged with driving the vehicle dangerously at the same location and time under Section 42(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987, read together with Section 34 of the Penal Code, which provides for a maximum of five years’ imprisonment and a fine of between RM5,000 and RM15,000.
They were also charged under Section 29(1) of the Minor Offences Act 1955 for failing to give a reasonable explanation for the possession of suspicious items, including two slings, a metal lock, an adjustable wrench, wire cutters, a steel hammer, a crowbar and chisel blades.
Also before Magistrate Tiong, Mohamad Danial Haiqal was charged individually with consuming amphetamine and methamphetamine on the same date and at the same location as Muhammad Putra Zulfaiz.
In the proceedings before Magistrate Siti Nur Ain, the court granted Muhammad Putra Zulfaiz bail of RM13,000, while Mohamad Danial Haiqal was granted bail of RM8,000 with one surety.
However, Judge Norshila and Magistrate Tiong did not grant bail to either accused due to the absence of a surety at today’s proceedings. All courts fixed Nov 26 for mention.
Deputy public prosecutors M. Ramanathan Alias Ashwin, Muhammad Aizudin Radthuan and Nadiah Malek Fauzie appeared for the prosecution.
Muhammad Putra Zulfaiz was represented by lawyer Daneish Thayalan and Mohamad Danial Haiqal by National Legal Aid Foundation lawyer Ernie Ahmad.
On Oct 11, police arrested both suspects after the vehicle they were travelling in crashed into several other private vehicles before being intercepted at the Jalan Jelatek–Jalan Taman Setiawangsa intersection here. — Bernama

Title: Police raid Melaka scam call centres targeting Chinese, Vietnamese victims, arrest 29
Article:
MELAKA, Oct 22 — Police crippled the activities of two call center syndicates suspected of being involved in online non-existent investment scams and love scams through two separate operations around Melaka Raya and Ayer Keroh, here.
Melaka Tengah District Police Chief ACP Halim Abas said that in the first operation on October 20, 14 Chinese nationals - comprising 11 men and three women aged between 21 and 52 - were arrested at four accommodation units in a hotel in Melaka Raya between 1pm and 3 pm.
“Initial investigations found that the premises were suspected of being used as a call center operations hub for online non-existent investment scam activities targeting Chinese nationals.
“The syndicate is believed to have started operating since mid-September, with the suspects acting as customer service officers to find and contact victims, as well as receiving a salary of about RM3,000,” he said at a press conference here today.
Halim added that police also seized 28 mobile phones of various brands, two laptops, a tablet, a translation device, five mobile phone farm charging/control hubs, 96 prepaid SIM cards, and RM6,400 in cash, with the total value of the seizures estimated at RM43,500.
Meanwhile, he said that in the second operation yesterday at about 3:00 pm, a premises at a resort around Ayer Keroh was raided, leading to the arrest of 15 men consisting of 14 Vietnamese nationals and one Chinese national aged between 21 and 40.
“Initial investigations found that the premises were suspected of being used as a call center operations hub for online scam activities using a love scam modus operandi targeting Vietnamese nationals.
“The syndicate is believed to have started operating since the beginning of this month, with the suspects playing the role of customer service officers to find and contact victims, as well as receiving a salary of about RM2,500,” he said.
Halim said police seized 11 sets of computers of various brands, 24 mobile phones, a Starlink router, a remote control set, a translation device, and 15 passport books, with the total value of the seizures estimated at RM43,400.
He added that four investigation papers were opened regarding the first operation, while one investigation paper was opened for the second operation.
All suspects are being investigated under Section 420 of the Penal Code as well as Section 6(1)© of the Immigration Act 1959/63 for offences related to personal identification documents.
“All suspects in the first operation have been remanded for four days from October 21 to 24, while the suspects in the second operation have been remanded for four days from October 22 to 25 to assist with the investigation,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Court of Appeal revokes bail for wheelchair-bound man charged with trafficking 6.2kg of cannabis
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Oct 22 — The Court of Appeal today overturned a High Court decision that had released a wheelchair-bound man on bail pending the disposal of his drug trafficking trial.
A three-man bench led by Justice Datuk Choo Kah Sing, alongside K. Muniandy and Datuk Seri Latifah Mohd Tahar, allowed the prosecution’s appeal to set aside the High Court’s ruling and ordered M. Alagesan to be remanded in custody.
Justice Choo, who delivered the unanimous decision, however, granted the defence’s application for Alagesan to be placed at the Sungai Buloh Hospital until the conclusion of his trial.
He held that the High Court judge erred in applying Section 388 of the Criminal Procedure Code to allow bail when there is an express law dealing with bail for drug trafficking offences.
He said the High Court’s decision was against the provision of Section 41B (1) (a) of the Dangerous Drugs Act, which states that bail shall not be granted to an accused person charged under the Act with an offence punishable by death or life imprisonment with not less than 12 strokes of the cane.
Justice Choo said Section 2 of the same Act stated that this subsection shall have the effect notwithstanding any written laws or any rule of law to the contrary.
The court ordered the RM150,000 bail deposited to be returned and revoked all previously imposed bail conditions.
“This court ordered the trial court to fix an early hearing date to complete the trial by the end of this year if possible considering the health condition of the accused,” Justice Choo said.
Earlier, lawyer Datuk Naran Singh, assisted by Amrick Singh Sandu, told the court that the trial dates have been scheduled for Feb 17 to 19 and March 24 to 26, 2027, and requested the court to issue a directive for the trial to be heard earlier.
Alagesan, 44, was charged with trafficking in 6.276 kg of cannabis at a house in Kg KL Tin Kalumpang, Kuala Kubu Baru, Hulu Selangor, Selangor on Feb 7, 2024.
On Sept 23, 2024, the Shah Alam High Court allowed Alagesan’s application to be released on bail pending disposal of his trial with RM150,000 with two sureties and imposed additional conditions including reporting to the nearest police station, surrendering his passport, and remaining at home from 7 pm to 7 am.
During proceedings, deputy public prosecutor Hafizah Johor Ariff Johor argued that Section 41B(1)(a) establishes a mandatory restriction that completely denies the right to bail for offences carrying the death penalty under the Dangerous Drugs Act, thereby divesting the High Court of any discretionary power to release the accused on bail pending completion of the trial.
She said that the High Court’s decision to grant bail in this case is a departure from established legal principles and it would open the door for thousands of detainees facing charges under Section 39B of the Dangerous Drug Act to apply for bail on subjective health grounds, thereby crippling Parliament’s intention to combat serious drug crimes.
In response, Naran Singh contended that despite the statutory prohibition under Section 41B, the court retains the inherent power to grant bail under exceptional circumstances.
He said Alagesan was paralysed from the waist down and was unable to squat, noting that standard prison toilets are equipped with squatting facilities. — Bernama

Title: Thunderstorms to lash Klang Valley, Penang, and six other states tonight
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 22 — The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) has issued a severe thunderstorm warning, forecasting heavy rain and strong winds across several states and federal territories until 9 pm today.
Issued at 5:50 pm, the alert covers the entire Klang Valley, including Kuala Lumpur, Selangor, and Putrajaya, alongside Penang.
Up north, the warning extends to Kedah (Sik, Kuala Muda, Baling, Kulim, and Bandar Baharu). Meanwhile, Perak is set to take a battering, with alerts plastered across Kerian, Selama, Larut Matang, Manjung, Bagan Datuk, Perak Tengah, Hilir Perak, Kampar, Kinta, and Kuala Kangsar.
Over in East Malaysia, Sarawak’s Limbang division is on high alert. In Sabah, the stormy weather targets the interior divisions of Sipitang, Tenom, and Pensiangan, sweeping across to the Sandakan division, which includes Tongod, Labuk, Sugut, and Kinabatangan.
The national weather bureau triggers these short-term alerts when radar detects imminent thunderstorms with rainfall intensity expected to exceed 20 millimetres per hour. These warnings are highly specific and valid for a maximum of six hours.
Residents in the affected zones should stay indoors, avoid parking in low-lying areas prone to flash floods, and steer clear of open spaces. Keep an eye on MetMalaysia’s official channels for real-time updates as the evening progresses.

Title: EC opens 30-day review of September 2026 supplementary electoral roll
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Oct 22 — The Supplementary Electoral Roll for September 2026 (DPT BLN9/2026) will be open for review for a period of 30 days, starting today until Nov 20, said Election Commission (EC) secretary Datuk Khairul Shahril Idrus.
He said the DPT BLN9/2026, which was gazetted today, includes 44,987 citizens aged 18 and above registered automatically as new voters between Sept 1 and Sept 30, 2026.
Additionally, the electoral roll contains 21,720 registered voters who have changed their electoral constituencies, as well as 4,805 voters who have undergone a change in their voter category or status.
“The Election Commission (EC) urges citizens aged 18 and above as of the period between September 1 and September 30, 2026 as well as any registered voters who have applied to change their electoral constituency, voter category, or status, to verify their names in the Supplementary Electoral Roll (DPT) for September 2026 (DPT BLN9/2026).
“Should they find that their names are not listed in the DPT BLN9/2026, they may file a claim by completing Form C via the online application at https://myspr.spr.gov.my, or by visiting the relevant State Election Office,” the statement said today.
He said verification can be conducted through four channels: the EC portal at https://www.spr.gov.my or https://myspr.spr.gov.my; the online application at https://myspr.spr.gov.my; the MySPR Semak mobile application; or by calling the Voter Registration Inquiry line at 03-8892 7218.
“Furthermore, any registered voter in a specific electoral constituency who, upon verification, wishes to object to the inclusion of a voter who has transferred into their constituency may do so by completing Form D via the online application at https://myspr.spr.gov.my, or by visiting the relevant State Election Office.
“Form C and Form D can also be downloaded from the EC portal at https://www.spr.gov.my. These must be submitted to the respective State Election Director, along with the payment of the required objection fee, during office hours on any working day throughout the verification period for the DPT BLN9/2026,” he said.
He said for any inquiries regarding the review of the Electoral Roll (DPT) for September 2026 (BLN9/2026), the public may visit the official Election Commission (EC) portal at https://www.spr.gov.my, contact the EC at 03-8892 7218, or reach out to any state election office. — Bernama

Title: Remand extended for suspect in AKPS officer’s murder at KLIA quarters
Article:
SEREMBAN, Oct 22 — The man suspected of murdering his wife, a Malaysian Border Control and Protection Agency (AKPS) officer, at their residential quarters near Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) in Nilai on Oct 15 has had his remand extended for another seven days.
Negeri Sembilan police chief Datuk Alzafny Ahmad said the suspect would remain in remand until Oct 29, while the case was being investigated under Section 302 of the Penal Code.
“The extended remand period begins today and runs until Oct 29,” he told reporters.
A post-mortem found that the woman died from pressure on her neck. The examination also revealed three stab wounds, two to the abdomen and one to the right cheek.
The woman, in her 30s, was found dead at the quarters after allegedly being stabbed by her husband, reportedly following a misunderstanding.
Police received a report on the incident at 9.30 pm after the husband surrendered at the Bandar Baru Salak Tinggi Police Station in Sepang, Selangor, and reported his wife’s death. — Bernama

Title: Maintain Western technology for DNB, says MP
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 22 — Wawasan information chief and Machang MP Wan Ahmad Fayhsal Wan Ahmad Kamal has urged Putrajaya to maintain Digital Nasional Bhd’s (DNB) Western technology stack, saying it is needed to balance the growing role of Chinese technology in Malaysia’s 5G and AI infrastructure.
Wan Fayhsal made the call in the Dewan Rakyat while Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, who is also the Tambun MP, was present in the chamber.
He said DNB’s Ericsson-based network was now Malaysia’s main Western technology counterweight, following U Mobile’s selection of Huawei for the country’s second 5G network.
He said the need to retain that balance had become more pressing as the government considers Huawei’s Ascend 910C chips for its proposed sovereign AI cloud, which could eventually handle sensitive government data.
“DNB was established by the Perikatan Nasional government in 2021. Now there are two paths, namely DNB with Ericsson and U Mobile with Huawei,” he said during his Budget 2027 debate.
“This is a good thing because Malaysia can benefit from Western and Eastern technology, as stressed by Tambun previously.”
Wan Fayhsal said Malaysia should not allow one technology ecosystem to become dominant across its critical digital infrastructure.
“I hope the government can retain both systems because, in my discussions with ambassadors from Europe and other Western countries, they want Malaysia to provide truly sovereign digital infrastructure so that they can invest in sensitive sectors,” he said.
The MP said keeping DNB on Western technology was therefore about more than 5G coverage or speed. It would give Malaysia and foreign investors a credible alternative for operations involving sensitive data.
He said the government’s proposed sovereign AI cloud made this consideration more urgent.
The government had announced a proposed RM2 billion allocation through the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) to establish the cloud under Budget 2026, with the initiative repeated in Budget 2027.
Wan Fayhsal said Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil had stated that work was under way to protect government data.
“Huawei Ascend 910C chips are being considered, and Telekom Malaysia (TM) has been selected to manage this project,” he said.
“The question is whether the government has carried out a risk assessment on the suppliers who will be used to handle national data.
“How will the government manage sensitivities related to digital sovereignty?”
He said the issue was whether Malaysia was building enough safeguards and alternatives as Chinese technology takes a greater role in the country’s digital ecosystem.
“The minister said work is ongoing to protect government data,” he said. “The government must explain whether it has conducted a risk assessment of the suppliers.”
Wan Fayhsal did not call for Chinese technology to be excluded. Instead, he said Malaysia should preserve both Western and Chinese technology pathways, so the country is not dependent on any one supplier or geopolitical bloc.
“Malaysia can benefit from Western and Eastern technology,” he said.
Maintaining DNB’s Ericsson-based stack, he added, would ensure that Malaysia retains a meaningful Western option while U Mobile’s Huawei-backed 5G network and the proposed sovereign AI cloud expand the role of Chinese technology in critical national infrastructure.

Title: Five days’ warning: New Malaysian model forecasts haze before it hits
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Oct 22 — Malaysia will introduce several transformative measures to strengthen efforts to tackle transboundary haze when it chairs the Sub-Regional Ministerial Steering Committee (MSC) on Transboundary Haze Pollution next year.
Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability Minister Datuk Seri Arthur Joseph Kurup said his ministry was conducting studies and drafting several new initiatives to ensure more effective and concrete action to address the recurring haze problem.
“Malaysia will take over the MSC chairmanship next year, and we are studying and planning several new initiatives to strengthen Asean-level efforts to tackle the haze problem.
“We hope to take more effective and concrete measures when we chair the MSC,” he told a press conference on the latest haze situation here today.
He said Malaysia proposed two key initiatives at the Asean ministerial meeting on July 9: science diplomacy, to ensure planning, action and spending to tackle haze are based on scientific data, enabling more targeted fire prevention and suppression efforts, and the setting up of a sustainable haze fund.
“The proposed sustainable haze fund, if approved, would serve as an Asean-level mechanism to help member states strengthen prevention, preparedness and monitoring measures,” he said.
He said most fires involved extremely dry peatland, where they could spread underground undetected for weeks or months, highlighting the need to study new technologies, including dry ice-based methods, to improve firefighting efforts.
In a related development, Arthur said Malaysia had also introduced the Malaysian Community Multiscale Air Quality Model (CMAQ), which can forecast potential air pollution and haze up to five days in advance.
He said the Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) had developed the platform to provide detailed air quality forecasts for Malaysia and the wider Southeast Asian region.
“We hope other countries will also adopt the system so that the public can plan and prepare up to five days in advance,” he said, adding that the platform began operating this year and is open to the public and Asean member states.
On the haze situation, Arthur said the transition to the Northeast Monsoon, expected to begin in late October, could alter the movement of transboundary haze currently affecting several areas in the south of the country, particularly Sarawak and Johor.
He said shifts in wind direction during the Northeast Monsoon could carry haze to other areas, easing its impact on areas currently affected, noting that haze drifting northwards from the south had significantly affected southern Sarawak, Johor and Singapore.
However, Arthur said Malaysia faced a greater risk of transboundary haze as the Super El Niño phenomenon was forecast to intensify from this month until January 2027, increasing the likelihood of forest and peatland fires in the region.
He said the El Niño phenomenon is expected to persist until mid-2027, with the year potentially among the hottest on record, bringing increasingly erratic rainfall, a higher risk of drought and more hotspots and fires that could worsen the haze.
“We also forecast that next year could be among the hottest on record, with temperature anomalies exceeding 2°C,” he said, adding that the government had taken into account the experience of the 2015-2016 Super El Niño, when rainfall decreased by up to 30 per cent in peninsular Malaysia and 45 per cent in Sabah.
He said prolonged hot and dry conditions would not only increase the risk of forest and peatland fires but could also affect agriculture, food security, water supplies and public health. — Bernama

Title: Iran warns it will hit US bases if Hormuz ship escorts continue
Article:
TEHRAN, Oct 22 — Iran’s Revolutionary Guards on Thursday threatened to strike American bases across the Middle East if the US military continues to escort ships through the Strait of Hormuz.
“The US military must know that if this trend continues, the conflict will extend to its bases in the region,” the Guards, the ideological arm of Iran’s military, said in a statement on their Sepah News website.
“This is a serious warning,” they added.
Iran claims control over Hormuz, a strategic shipping route through which one-fifth of the world’s oil supplies passed before war broke out in February.
It regularly attacks ships that attempt to navigate the strait without its authorisation.
But the US military has been escorting vessels through the waterway in increasing numbers, with Iran responding by stepping up attacks.
Four ships were hit in the area overnight as they attempted to pass through the wider Gulf, Iranian forces said on Thursday.
Washington has also been maintaining a naval blockade on Iranian ports in an attempt to squeeze the country’s economy, while negotiations to end the conflict are deadlocked.
Hormuz, bordered to the north by Iran and to the south by Oman, is only about 30 kilometres (19 miles) wide at its narrowest point and is a critical route for ships carrying oil and gas from energy-rich Gulf countries. — AFP

Title: Snip, snip, slip through? Wire fences cut at illegal crossings near Rantau Panjang-Thai border
Article:
PASIR MAS, Oct 22 — Eleven police reports regarding damage to concertina wire fences at 13 illegal crossing points around Rantau Panjang were recorded between March 27 and October 12.
Bukit Aman Internal Security and Public Order Department (PGA) Deputy Director Datuk Suzrin Mohamad Rodhi said the damage was believed to have been deliberately done to open up pathways for smuggling activities and cross-border crimes.
He added that the records of the PGA Southeast Brigade up to October 22 showed that the damage involved cutting, vandalising, and sabotaging the fences, with the damaged length estimated to be between two and five metres at each location.
“Any individuals detected committing the offence will be arrested, and further legal action will be taken,” he told reporters after conducting an inspection at an illegal crossing point near Jeram Perdah, Rantau Panjang, here, today.
Suzrin said his team constantly updates field information alongside the National Security Council and the police contingent regarding fence-cutting incidents in the border areas.
He added that on-duty personnel also took the initiative to tie back or repair the damaged fences to restore security control at the affected locations, in addition to channelling information to relevant parties for continuous monitoring.
“Enforcement actions are also being carried out by the PGA together with the relevant District Police Headquarters to address these incidents and ensure that border security remains preserved,” he said. — Bernama
* Editor’s note: PGA stands for Pasukan Gerakan Am, or the General Operations Force.

Title: No drones without approval, Melaka police tell election candidates
Article:
MELAKA, Oct 22 — Candidates and political parties intending to use drones during the Melaka State Election campaign must first obtain approval from the relevant authorities and cannot deploy the devices indiscriminately.
Melaka police chief Datuk Dzulkhairi Mukhtar said drone operations were subject to regulatory controls by the relevant authorities, including the Civil Aviation Authority of Malaysia (CAAM).
“Political parties cannot simply use equipment such as drones, as approval from the relevant agencies is required.
“Even the police must obtain approval before using drones for operational purposes,” he told reporters after attending a briefing on the 16th Melaka State Election for political party representatives at the Melaka Police Contingent Headquarters here today.
He said Melaka police would deploy about 3,400 personnel to ensure security and public order throughout the election period, including an additional 1,500 personnel from outside the state to support operations.
“The deployment of these reinforcements will be coordinated by Bukit Aman.
“The police will also use technology, including closed-circuit television (CCTV) cameras and drones operated by a special team, to help ensure the smooth conduct of the election,” he said.
Dzulkhairi also reminded all political parties and candidates to avoid raising issues involving race, religion and royalty (3R), spreading defamatory allegations or engaging in actions that could disrupt public order during the campaign period, which begins on Oct 31.
“The police will remain vigilant on matters concerning security and public order, while issues involving 3R and social media content will be referred to the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) for investigation,” he said.
He said police had so far received two reports involving political parties, lodged on Oct 14, concerning the vehicle-free zone in Banda Hilir and an issue involving a Rohingya ethnic school, even though the nomination process had yet to take place.
“Both cases are still under investigation under Section 500 of the Penal Code and Section 233 of the Communications and Multimedia Act 1998,” he said.
In a related development, Dzulkhairi said a total of 2,764 early voters, including postal voters from the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM), had been recorded for the Melaka state election scheduled for Nov 10.
Earlier, 140 political party representatives from across Melaka attended the briefing, which also involved representatives from MCMC and the Election Commission (EC).
Dzulkhairi said the briefing was aimed at helping political parties understand the procedures and regulations they must comply with throughout the election period, including requirements for campaign permits.
“For permit applications, the police will call in candidates’ representatives according to their respective districts to facilitate early applications, making it easier to conduct campaign activities,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Pay up or go to jail: 43 fined for using other people’s Malaysian ID cards in Johor Bahru
Article:
JOHOR BAHRU, Oct 22 — A total of 43 individuals, including three Malaysians, were fined between RM1,000 and RM9,000 by three Magistrates’ Courts here today for using forged identity cards or copies of identity cards belonging to other people.
Of the total, 35 were charged with using copies of other people’s identity cards, while the remaining eight were charged with using forged identity cards as personal identification documents.
The accused, aged between 18 and 49, comprised three Malaysians and foreign nationals from Indonesia and the Philippines.
They were sentenced after pleading guilty to the charges, which were read out separately before Magistrates Nurzihan Abdul Rehman, A. Shaarmini and Atifah Hazimah Wahab.
The courts also ordered them to serve jail terms ranging from one to six months if they failed to pay their respective fines.
The offences were committed at two factories, Gorin Technical Industry (Malaysia) Sdn Bhd and Masimo Medical Technologies (M) Sdn Bhd, located in the MIEL and Pasir Gudang industrial areas, between 10 am and 8 pm on Oct 20.
The charges were framed under Regulation 25(1)(e) of the National Registration Regulations 1990 (2007 Amendment), which provides for a maximum jail term of three years, a fine of up to RM20,000, or both upon conviction.
The prosecution was conducted by National Registration Department prosecuting officers Mohd Ramzi Adnan, Noorleelawathi Man and Md Shahedan Md Taib.
Ten of the accused were represented by lawyers Amir Haikal, Jackson Danial, Heng Wang Qian Wei, Rashidah Baharom and Muhd Akmal Mazlan, while the remaining accused were unrepresented. — Bernama

Title: Do Malaysians know MA63? Communications Ministry may run a study to find out
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 22 — The Communications Ministry is considering conducting a dedicated study to gauge public understanding of the Malaysia Agreement 1963 (MA63) and the history of Malaysia’s formation.
Deputy Communications Minister Teo Nie Ching said neither the ministry nor its agencies, including the Malaysian Information Department (Japen), had conducted a baseline study for this purpose.
She said she was prepared to bring the proposal to the ministry and Japen for further consideration.
“At present, neither RTM nor Japen has conducted a survey to measure public understanding of MA63 and the formation of Malaysia.
“I will bring the proposal back to the ministry for further discussion with Japen to determine whether the department can conduct the survey,” she said during the question-and-answer session in the Dewan Rakyat today.
She was responding to a supplementary question from Isnaraissah Munirah Majilis (Warisan-Kota Belud) on whether the ministry was prepared to conduct a perception study to gauge public understanding, particularly in the Peninsula, of Sabah and Sarawak’s rights under MA63.
On existing public information efforts, Teo said Japen had uploaded 115 posts, including 21 creative content pieces, on its official social media channels about the formation of Malaysia and the implementation of MA63. — Bernama
* Editor’s note: Japen stands for Jabatan Penerangan Malaysia in Malay, or the Malaysian Information Department in English.

Title: Haze row: Malaysia to take transboundary pollution to Asean meeting in Manila
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Oct 22 — Malaysia urges Indonesia to take firm and effective action to tackle fires contributing to transboundary haze pollution, which is affecting air quality and public well-being in Malaysia.
Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability Minister Datuk Seri Arthur Joseph Kurup said Malaysia respected its good diplomatic relations with Indonesia but reserved the right to demand appropriate action to ensure its people could enjoy clean air.
“Malaysia’s stance is clear.
“We respect our good relations with Indonesia, but we also have the right to demand effective action when cross-border pollution affects our people.
“The fires must be controlled, pollution must be reduced and the people must be protected,” he said at a press conference on the latest haze developments here today.
Arthur said Malaysia had held several consultations with Indonesia and offered assistance, including assets and personnel, to expedite firefighting efforts in affected areas.
He said the offer was also conveyed by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim to Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto.
Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi also raised the matter during his official visit to Indonesia.
Arthur said Indonesia had verbally agreed to accept Malaysia’s assistance, but further coordination was still underway pending authorisation for the deployment of assets and personnel.
He said Malaysia would raise the transboundary haze issue at the Asean Foreign Ministers’ Meeting in Manila, the Philippines, early next month to seek a more effective regional solution.
The government would study the outcome of the meeting before determining its next steps, he added.
Arthur said satellite reports on Oct 14 showed widespread clusters of hotspots in southern Sumatra, as well as West Kalimantan, Central Kalimantan and South Kalimantan.
He stressed the importance of regional cooperation to ensure fires were controlled at source and prevent haze pollution from continuing to affect neighbouring countries. — Bernama

Title: TalentCorp business as usual, says HR Ministry, as it lodges reports on alleged interference
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 22 — The Human Resources Ministry (Kesuma) has lodged several official reports with the authorities over alleged attempts to interfere with an ongoing review and investigation at Talent Corporation Malaysia Berhad (TalentCorp).
In a statement today, the ministry said the alleged interference involved spreading misleading information, influencing individuals within the agency, and diverting attention from matters under scrutiny.
It said such actions could undermine the integrity and independence of the review and investigation.
The reports were lodged following the receipt of information and evidence to allow the authorities to conduct a more appropriate and independent investigation.
“Kesuma will leave it entirely to the authorities to examine the evidence, establish the facts and take appropriate legal action if warranted,” the statement said.
Kesuma and TalentCorp are undertaking organisational reforms to strengthen the agency’s transparency, integrity and accountability.
A joint review by TalentCorp’s management and the ministry identified several areas requiring improvement, including provisions in the company’s constitution, compliance with internal policies, internal controls, and integrity and accountability mechanisms.
Kesuma stressed that the review must proceed independently, transparently and without undue interference or influence.
It said it would not tolerate attempts to exploit positions, influence or connections to compromise the process.
“The review and related investigations also involve TalentCorp employees and management. All parties must cooperate fully to ensure the process is conducted fairly and objectively.
“Any further action will be determined by the findings of the review and investigations,” it said.
Kesuma said TalentCorp’s operations and strategic programmes would continue as usual throughout the process, with the agency to remain focused on its national talent development mandate, including improving graduate employability, developing future-ready skills and strengthening workforce participation. — Bernama
* Editor’s note: Kesuma stands for Kementerian Sumber Manusia, or the Human Resources Ministry.

Title: Court grants Perikatan stay on RoS deregistration, allows coalition to contest Melaka state polls
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 22 — The High Court here today allowed Perikatan Nasional’s (PN) application to stay the Registrar of Societies’ (RoS) decision to revoke the coalition’s registration pending the outcome of its judicial review.
Judge Datuk Azizan Md Arshad also granted PN’s application to stay the enforcement of an RoS notice suspending all activities of the political coalition.
The decision allows PN to continue its political activities, including contesting the Melaka state election scheduled for November 14.
In his judgment, Azizan said there were exceptional circumstances warranting the stay, taking into account the applicants’ involvement in political activities and their rights as party members, elected representatives and Members of Parliament, as submitted by their counsel.
“The court finds that no prejudice will arise if this stay is granted, as the political activities of the applicants or Perikatan Nasional can continue to be monitored, and enforcement action can be taken if any activities are found to contravene the laws of the country.
“Therefore, the application for a stay of execution is granted until the full disposal of the substantive hearing of this judicial review,” he said. — Bernama

Title: MyEG suspension to continue as RM314m outstanding payment remains unsettled, says Loke
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 22 — Transport Minister Anthony Loke Siew Fook today said the outstanding payment MyEG Services Bhd (MyEG) owes the government has yet to be settled, following the suspension of the company’s services as a Road Transport Department (JPJ) collection agent earlier this month.
MyEG is a digital and e-government services provider that was previously tasked with collecting JPJ-related payments.
He said the suspension had not disrupted public access to JPJ services, as motorists could continue using alternative channels, including the MyJPJ application, to access their information and carry out transactions.
“There has been no disruption to services because JPJ is handling the matter. The public can use MyJPJ and easily access their information.
“As for the payment, it has not been made yet,” he told reporters after launching the Masjid Jamek LRT station beautification project here today.
JPJ suspended the services of MyEG Sdn Bhd and Zetrix AI Bhd, both under the MyEG Group, effective October 5 after the companies failed to remit RM314 million in government revenue collected between May 19 and September 30.
The outstanding amount comprises revenue collected on behalf of the government that had not been transferred to the Transport Ministry’s main collection account.
Loke had previously said the ministry would only consider an application to resume operations after the full outstanding amount had been paid.
The government took action after the companies failed to settle the arrears despite receiving 35 reminder notices and participating in engagement sessions with the authorities since May.
Despite the suspension, JPJ has assured the public that its services remain available through alternative channels, including the MyJPJ application, JPJ Public Portal, counters and kiosks.
The suspension covers JPJ services previously offered through the MyEG Group, including transactions involving road tax, driving licences and traffic summonses.
The ministry and JPJ have also said they would take appropriate legal action to recover the outstanding government revenue.
Note: The Road Transport Department (RTD) is known as Jabatan Pengangkutan Jalan (JPJ) in Malay.

Title: Kuching school attack probe ongoing, police to hold press conference on Oct 27
Article:
KUCHING, Oct 22 — Police are gathering and verifying information as investigations into the alleged attack on a female teacher at an international school here yesterday morning continue.
According to the Sarawak Police Contingent Headquarters, the investigation team is carrying out various investigative measures to ensure the accuracy of the information obtained.
In a statement, the contingent said the investigation is ongoing and a press conference is scheduled for October 27, with the time to be announced later.
Media representatives with questions were advised to channel them to the contingent beforehand to allow the relevant parties to prepare accurate and comprehensive answers.
Police are investigating a case involving a 16-year-old male student who allegedly attacked a teacher with an axe at an international school here.
Yesterday, acting Sarawak Police Commissioner DCP Saifullizan Ishak said police received a report of the incident at 8.03am via the MERS 999 emergency line.
The teacher reportedly suffered injuries to her hand during the incident.
Saifullizan said the case is being investigated under Section 324 of the Penal Code for voluntarily causing hurt by dangerous weapons or means, as well as Section 6(1) of the Explosives Act 1957. — The Borneo Post

Title: Loke welcomes RM5m Masjid Jamek LRT makeover, wants stations to drive local economy
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 22 — Transport Minister Anthony Loke Siew Fook today welcomed a RM5 million beautification project at the Masjid Jamek LRT station, saying the busy interchange should be more than a transit point and help drive economic activity and tourism in the capital.
Loke said the station, which serves thousands of commuters and sits close to historic attractions in the city, was an important gateway for both locals and tourists.
“Every ringgit spent must bring tangible benefits to the people. We want to ensure that the improvements go beyond making the station look beautiful, and genuinely improve comfort, safety and convenience for users.
“Public transport stations should not merely be places where passengers board and alight from trains, but should also become centres for community activities, commerce and tourism,” he said at the launch of the project today.
The project, launched by Prasarana Malaysia Berhad in collaboration with Think City, is the third phase of efforts to rejuvenate the station and its surrounding area, with works expected to be completed by the end of 2027.
Transport Minister Anthony Loke during the launch of the LRT Masjid Jamek Station Beautification Project in Kuala Lumpur October 22, 2026. — Picture by Firdaus Latif
The RM5 million investment covers four main components: upgrading the area around Jalan Benteng with public and commercial spaces, improving lighting along Jalan Tun Perak, adding greenery to the station platforms and improving wayfinding around the station.
Loke said the improvements were timely, given that Masjid Jamek was a major interchange connecting the Kelana Jaya Line with the Ampang/Sri Petaling Line, serving an average of 1.39 million passengers a month.
He also joked that its proximity to Dataran Merdeka made it particularly busy during demonstrations, but stressed that its importance extended beyond its role in the city’s transport network.
The area holds historical significance as the meeting point of the Klang and Gombak rivers, which marked the beginning of Kuala Lumpur’s development.
Loke said the station was also an important gateway to nearby heritage attractions, including Dataran Merdeka, the Sultan Abdul Samad Building and Sultan Abdul Samad Jamek Mosque.
He said the beautification project supported the government’s Warisan Kuala Lumpur (Warisan KL) initiative to strengthen the capital’s heritage appeal while connecting public transport users to cultural attractions and commercial activities.
Transport Minister Anthony Loke poses for a picture during the launch of the LRT Masjid Jamek Station Beautification Project in Kuala Lumpur October 22, 2026. — Picture by Firdaus Latif
Loke also expressed support for plans to introduce more commercial spaces at stations, saying these could create business opportunities, generate income and encourage more people to use public transport.
He said such spaces could also provide opportunities for local businesses and brands to showcase Malaysian products and flavours, rather than being dominated by international brands.
“We want to see how public transport stations can be transformed from transit points into catalysts for the economy,” he said.
Loke added that improving connectivity beyond stations was equally important in encouraging public transport use, particularly through more covered walkways linking stations to surrounding areas.
He welcomed efforts under Budget 2027 to increase covered walkways in Kuala Lumpur, saying Prasarana and Kuala Lumpur City Hall (DBKL) should work together to identify gaps and ensure pedestrians could move between transport hubs and nearby destinations more seamlessly.
He said he had also instructed Prasarana to provide the Transport Ministry with weekly reports on station facilities, including the number of faulty escalators and lifts that were out of service.
Loke said station facilities must remain in good condition to ensure a comfortable and reliable journey, adding that the passenger experience should cover the entire trip, from the station entrance to the final destination.
Prasarana said the beautification project had been implemented in phases since 2025 and was expected to turn Masjid Jamek into a greener, more user-friendly space with improved commercial facilities, strengthening its role as a community, tourism and commercial hub in central Kuala Lumpur.

Title: Bandar Kuching MP urges public to stop sharing Kuching school attack videos, warns of copycat effect
Article:
KUCHING, Oct 22 — Bandar Kuching MP Dr Kelvin Yii Lee Wuen has urged the public and the media to stop sharing videos of a school violence incident in Kuching, warning that such exposure can lead to a copycat effect.
The incident, which occurred yesterday at an international school, involved a 16-year-old student injuring a teacher.
“I appeal to everyone, including the media, to stop sharing videos, images, notes or details of this act,” Dr Yii said in a statement.
“Research on school violence overseas shows that widely publicised attacks are often followed by similar incidents.”
He noted that when an attack is livestreamed and shared thousands of times, the attacker gains the notoriety he may have been seeking.
“Every share, however well-meaning, puts more children in danger,” he added.
Dr Yii also pointed to a troubling rise in violent incidents involving students since the killing of a student in Bandar Utama in October 2025.
He stressed that while guards, fences, and bag checks have their place, they cannot address the negative material children are exposed to online.
“If we ignore this factor, we will keep responding to tragedies instead of preventing them,” he said.
The MP highlighted that he has consistently pushed for stronger online regulations in Parliament.
He noted that just two days before the Kuching incident, he asked the Communications Ministry if the government would extend social media age limits to online gaming platforms.
While he welcomed the ministry’s ongoing studies and public consultations on a new Gaming Sub-Code, he stressed that these efforts must be matched with urgency.
Citing Australia’s experience, Dr Yii said age limits alone are easily bypassed, pointing out that over eight in ten children under 16 there still use social media despite a ban.
“As we roll out our own measures, we must place a firm duty of care on platforms,” he said, urging them to design safer services and stop algorithms from amplifying harmful content.
Dr Yii also addressed the cruelty the young suspect faced online prior to the incident, noting that constant mockery from strangers can push youth toward harming themselves or others.
He emphasised that the teenager is a minor whose identity must be protected, adding that he should be dealt with through legal and rehabilitative processes rather than an online mob.
He called for stronger mental health support and early intervention in schools to recognise warning signs before it is too late.
Furthermore, Dr Yii called on the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) to play a more proactive role by working with platforms to detect and block re-uploads of violent footage immediately, rather than waiting for complaints.
He suggested establishing a rapid-response protocol for school-related incidents to contain harmful material in the critical first hours.
Dr Yii also urged online news portals and social media page owners to prioritise responsibility over viewership.
“What is the point of higher viewership and ratings if the price is making our schools less safe?” he questioned.
The MP added that he has spoken to Deputy Communications Minister Teo Nie Ching and urged the Malaysian Media Council to establish clear guidelines on reporting such incidents.
“Protecting our children is a shared duty of government, platforms, schools, parents, the media and every one of us who scrolls, comments and shares,” he said.

Title: RM1,000 aid lands just in time for Deepavali for 400 Negeri Sembilan taxi drivers
Article:
SEREMBAN, Oct 22 — The RM1,000 special financial assistance from the Madani Government has brought relief to more than 400 taxi and hire car drivers in Negeri Sembilan, particularly those celebrating Deepavali, by helping them prepare for the festival, Transport Minister Anthony Loke said.
He said the aid would help reduce recipients’ financial burden, allowing them to meet the costs of Deepavali preparations and their families’ daily needs.
“The RM1,000 may not resolve every problem or fully cover vehicle maintenance costs.
“However, I hope the assistance will go some way towards easing their daily expenses, helping them buy groceries, replace tyres or refuel their vehicles so they can continue earning a living.
“I promised earlier that the assistance would be delivered before Deepavali.
“Today, I am handing it over ahead of the festival so that you can put it towards your Deepavali expenses,” he said at a ceremony for taxi, hire car and school bus drivers at the Seremban City Council Hall today.
Loke said the next phase of the assistance would be paid directly into the bank accounts of other eligible recipients nationwide through electronic funds transfer.
He said the Ministry of Transport (MOT) would continue supporting taxi drivers through its transformation programme to keep them competitive in the public transport industry, including by working with Proton to lower the cost of new vehicles and providing financing facilities and rebates to ease their financial burden.
He said more than 100 vehicles had been booked under the programme, which seeks to boost drivers’ earnings by offering advertising space inside vehicles and using apps to connect them with passengers.
In a related development, Loke said the government would continue to issue special vehicle registration number series, typically two to three a year, but had no plans to introduce numbers featuring specific names or words, opting to retain the existing alphanumeric system.
Loke said the MOT had decided to retain the country’s long-standing vehicle registration system, despite the potential for personalised number plates to generate additional government revenue.
Meanwhile, taxi driver L. Jagathesan, 68, who has worked in the industry for 30 years, said the incentive was the biggest he had received and would go towards his Deepavali expenses.
Port Dickson taxi driver M. Selvaraju, 66, who has worked in the industry for 37 years, said he appreciated the government’s gesture towards taxi drivers and hoped similar efforts would continue.
Driver Muhammad Auzai Azman, 28, who has been in the profession for two years, said the assistance helped drivers like him meet their daily needs. — Bernama

Title: Why your air quality app and the official API don’t match, environment minister explains in Parliament
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 22 — The Air Pollutant Index (API) readings issued by the Department of Environment (DOE) remain the government’s official reference for determining air quality and managing haze.
Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability Minister Datuk Seri Arthur Joseph Kurup said the official API was calculated based on the concentrations of six major pollutants monitored around the clock through 68 automatic air quality monitoring stations nationwide.
He said the stations used measurement equipment and technical methods recognised by the United States Environmental Protection Agency, with procedures in place to ensure the accuracy and reliability of the data.
“Station operations include equipment maintenance, calibration, instrument performance checks and quality assurance procedures to ensure that the data used to calculate the official API are accurate and reliable,” he said during the Minister’s Question Time in the Dewan Rakyat today.
Arthur was answering a question from Manndzri Nasib (BN-Tenggara), who wanted to know how the government ensured that Malaysia’s official API readings were accurate, transparent and trusted by the public.
He said the stations operated under a Quality Assurance Project Plan (QAPP), which included daily automated zero and span checks, periodic calibration using standard gases traceable to international metrology standards under the National Institute of Standards and Technology, and regular performance audits.
Data collected were also monitored continuously through the Environmental Data Centre to detect changes in readings, assess equipment performance and enable corrective action in the event of disruptions or irregularities.
Arthur said the official API was updated hourly, while the calculations for PM2.5 and PM10 were based on their 24-hour moving average concentrations, in line with World Health Organisation standards and practices adopted by international environmental agencies.
On differences between official API readings and those displayed on platforms such as the Air Quality Index (AQI) and other independent applications, he said these did not necessarily mean that the official readings were inaccurate.
“Differences may arise because these platforms use different scales, thresholds, categories, averaging periods, update times and data sources,” he said, adding that some also relied on low-cost sensors or estimates derived from models and satellite data.
He explained that satellite data measured particle concentrations in the atmosphere rather than actual air quality at ground level, where people breathe.
Such readings could also be affected by cloud cover and atmospheric humidity.
Meanwhile, Arthur said the ministry was open to improving the National Haze Action Plan to ensure that coordination mechanisms and protective measures remained relevant as haze conditions changed.
“This is important to ensure that the actions of the various agencies are better coordinated, particularly when API readings reach unhealthy or very unhealthy levels, to protect public health and well-being,” he said.
On measures to address haze and open burning, Arthur said the government maintained a zero-tolerance approach towards open burning.
The DOE had taken 3,433 enforcement actions related to open-burning incidents between August and October this year, he added. — Bernama

Title: Nine charged with being members of ‘Geng Suria’ crime group in Sungai Petani
Article:
SUNGAI PETANI, Oct 22 — Nine men were charged in the Sessions Court here today with being members of an organised crime group known as the ‘Geng Suria’.
They are Thayalan, 28; A. Tana Balan, 30; Muhamad Rizwan Abd Jalil, 28; G. Sritharan, 39; B. Saranraj, 38; A. Simon, 34; G. Suria Prasad (alleged to be the gang leader), 30; A. Suresh, 52; and Kavines, 31.
No pleas were recorded after the charges were read out in Tamil before Judges Nabisha Ibrahim and Najwa Che Mat in separate courtrooms, as the case falls under the jurisdiction of the High Court.
The nine men are charged with being members of the organised crime group at an unnumbered house on Jalan Sekerat, Pekan Lama, here, between December 2024 and April this year.
The charge, framed under Section 130V(1) of the Penal Code, provides imprisonment of up to 20 years upon conviction.
The prosecution was conducted by Deputy Public Prosecutors Yazid Mustaqim Roslan and Mohd Fakhrurrazi Ahmad Salim.
Lawyer S. Sagthiyaraj represented Saranraj and Thayalan, while lawyer Mohammad Naim Kamaruddin represented Sritharan, Simon, and Tana Balan.
The remaining four accused were unrepresented.
The court denied bail to all nine accused and set Nov 17 for mention. — Bernama

Title: Malaysia eyes bigger role in Turkmenistan’s oil and gas sector
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 22 — Malaysia is strengthening its energy partnership with Turkmenistan to unlock new commercial opportunities for companies, particularly in higher-value oil and gas services, technology and specialised engineering, said Economy Minister Akmal Nasrullah Mohd Nasir.
“Our companies are ready to work with Turkmenistan partners not only as suppliers, but as long-term collaborators committed to local value creation,” the minister said in his remarks during the opening plenary of the Oil and Gas of Turkmenistan 2026 in Ashgabat.
The three-day OGT 2026, which began on Oct 21, brought together 20 Malaysian oil and gas services and equipment (OGSE) companies, including Petroliam Nasional Bhd (Petronas), according to a statement by the Economy Ministry today.
Of these, seven exhibitors were at the inaugural Malaysia Pavilion, under the National OGSE Industry Blueprint 2021-2030’s International Market Access Programme led by Malaysia Petroleum Resources Corporation (MPRC).
The ministry said the engagement builds on Petronas’ 30-year presence in Turkmenistan and follows the formalisation of the Framework Agreement on Long-Term Cooperation for the Development of Hydrocarbon Resources in Turkmenistan during Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim’s official visit in June 2026.
“Industry cooperation is set to be further strengthened through a memorandum of understanding between MPRC and (Turkmenistan’s national oil company) State Concern Turkmennebit, scheduled to be signed today, to facilitate collaboration in OGSE in Turkmenistan,” it said.
As part of the visit, Akmal Nasrullah is scheduled to hold bilateral meetings with Turkmenistan’s Deputy Chairman of the Cabinet of Ministers Guvanch Agajanov, State Minister and SC Turkmengas chairman Maksat Babayev, Finance and Economy Minister Mammetguly Astanagulov, and the leadership of Dragon Oil and Eni Turkmenistan Ltd to strengthen bilateral economic ties and explore strategic collaboration.
“These engagements will build the momentum for the Malaysia-Turkmenistan Energy Cooperation Roundtable, bringing together Malaysian OGSE companies and Turkmenistan’s key stakeholders, including Turkmengas and Turkmennebit.
“The roundtable is expected to translate shared interests into concrete cooperation focusing on high-value services, technology transfer and skills development, in line with the 13th Malaysia Plan (2026-2030),” the ministry added. — Bernama
